text:
raj: alert from gateway-alerts: sudden spike in 5xx and request timeouts from serving cluster eu-west-1. error rate > 12% for last 3m, p95 latency climbing. paging SRE oncall :rotating_light:

sre-oncall-bot: Paging @sre-oncall (severity: P1) — elevated 5xx + timeouts affecting multiple customers. Incident channel created. thread_ts=2109876543

maria: I'm on it, grabbing logs and routing tables. are we seeing queue depth growth on the scheduler?

alex: yes — scheduler.metrics.batch_queue_depth jumped from ~120 to ~4.2k over 2m. KV cache misses increased too. looks like batching backlog -> HOL blocking.

jen: customers reporting API 504s in status page. Support says two larger customers saw spikes around the time window. @support_lead any details?

support_lead: confirmed — customer alpha and beta had increased errors and timeouts. Support opened tickets. Notified account teams.

raj: quick triage: is this capacity saturation or a bad request pattern? any sudden traffic shift?

alex: traffic spike ~3x usual for that cluster — but also many long-context requests (seq len > 8k) which balloon per-request token cost. combined with batching heuristics, we've hit a scheduling hotspot.

maria: reproducing locally: when large sequences join small ones, batch packs and prevents progress -> head-of-line. We need rapid mitigation: reduce max_batch_size, enable per-request routing to large-context pool, or fallback to smaller model variant.

jen: prioritization: keep customers alive. Proposed immediate actions: 1) enable short-term restrictive backpressure (reject huge seq-length requests with 429) 2) scale up dedicated capacity in eu-west-1 if possible 3) fallback non-blocking route to lower-cap model for latency-sensitive traffic.

alex: I can flip backpressure rules on the gateway. Command:

```
# toggle per-route backpressure
redwoodctl routes update --region eu-west-1 --route /v1/generate --backpressure=reject_large_seq
```

I also recommend reducing batch_window to 10ms to avoid long waits.

maria: I'm tailing scheduler logs. patch to lower batch_window in prod runtime: `PATCH /runtime/configs/global` payload: `{\"batch_window_ms\":10}` — planning to apply to the affected pool.

raj: do it. apply backpressure first so we don't ramp errors while config lands.

alex: applied gateway rule. starting to see a drop in incoming long-context requests being accepted. queue depth down to ~900. errors still elevated but trending down. :thumbsup:

sre-oncall-bot: automated note: error budget burn detected. Alert suppression set for 10m while mitigation is in progress.

maria: pushed runtime config to eu-west-1 pool. batch_window at 10ms. batcher logs show fewer giant batches, preemptive eviction enabled for sequences > 4k.

jen: checking customer impact: support says alpha errors down ~60% after the gateway change. beta still seeing intermittent 504s.

alex: beta routes heavily to a single scheduler shard that still has hot KV cache miss ratio. investigating data skew. I can kick a graceful restart on that shard to clear state and rebalance.

raj: plan: (A) graceful restart the hot shard (alex) (B) continue backpressure (alex) (C) open fallback routing policy to use small-llm for latency-sensitive customers (maria) (D) keep support loop updated (jen). Anyone object?

jen: go ahead. notify account teams about the restart window (2 min).

alex: performing graceful restart now: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/scheduler-shard-17 -n redwood-eu`

sre-oncall-bot: deploybot: rollout of scheduler-shard-17 started by alex. monitor for failures.

alex: shard came back in ~90s, health checks passed. batch_queue_depth for that shard dropped from ~2.1k to ~120. overall cluster queue now ~250.

maria: opened temporary route rule: `--fallback-model small-llm-v2` for customers with SLA latency <500ms. Applied to alpha and beta.

support_lead: alpha and beta both report dramatic improvement post-fallback. alpha fully recovered, beta 90% recovered. ongoing checks for edge cases.

raj: good. next: we need a post-incident action item list: 1) adjust batching heuristic to segregate long-context flows automatically 2) add per-shard cache warming on scaling events 3) add circuit-breaker to reject heavy sequences before they hit scheduler. 4) incident blameless writeup.

jen: I'll create an incident ticket and assign follow-ups. linking customer tickets and SLA impact.

alex: metrics show p95 latency back to baseline, 5xx down to ~0.8%. keeping monitoring enhanced for 30m.

maria: also instrumented a quick guard in routing that will route requests with seq_len > 6k to a dedicated long-context pool — feature flag enabled for 1h to observe.

sre-oncall-bot: incident severity downgraded to P2 based on recovery and customer reports.

raj: handoff: I'm going offline in 20m. @maria will be primary for the next 2 hours for verification and follow-up. maria, confirm you accept handoff.

maria: accepted. I'll monitor and validate the long-context feature flag, confirm cache warming, and coordinate with infra on capacity.

jen: updating status page: note that we experienced elevated 5xx/timeouts due to scheduler backlog caused by mix of large-context requests and batching behavior; mitigations applied and customers recovered; postmortem TBD.

support_lead: notifying account teams and PS for any follow-ups.

alex: leaving a snapshot of useful logs and commands in the thread for follow-up:

```
# useful queries
kubectl -n redwood-eu logs deploy/scheduler-shard-17 --since=15m | jq '. | {ts, event, batch_size}'
redwoodctl metrics query --cluster eu-west-1 --metric batch_queue_depth --window 30m
```

maria: summary: root cause = scheduler saturation from long-context request surge + batching policy creating HOL blocking. Immediate mitigations = gateway backpressure, reduce batch window, shard restart, fallback routing. Next steps = heuristic changes, cache warming, circuit-breaker, postmortem.

raj: thanks team. keeping the channel open for the next checks. will close after 60m if stable. :white_check_mark:
